```{python}
np.random.seed(3)

PROJECT_DIR = Path("/Users/daniel/PhD/spectral-comparison/code/")
DATA_PATH_IEEG = PROJECT_DIR / "data/Frauscher2018"
DATA_PATH_SOURCES = PROJECT_DIR / "data/Mantini2018"

fig_dir = Path("figures/chapter2/uncorrected")
fig_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
CACHE_DIR = Path("_cache")
CACHE_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# Scatter + overlap use the full 0.5-80 Hz range; the cortical maps slice to
# >=1 Hz (HD sources were high-pass filtered at 1 Hz). Single gamma 30-80 Hz.
FREQ_RANGE = (0.5, 80.0)
MAP_FMIN = 1.0
MAP_BANDS = [
    ("δ", 1.0, 4.0),
    ("θ", 4.0, 8.0),
    ("α", 8.0, 13.0),
    ("β", 13.0, 30.0),
    ("γ", 30.0, 80.0),
]
MAP_BAND_ORDER = [b[0] for b in MAP_BANDS]


def _is_float_str(s) -> bool:
    try:
        float(s)
        return True
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return False


def cache_csv(name: str, build) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Load a PSD table from `_cache/<name>.csv`, or compute it with `build`.

    Float-named frequency columns are written as string headers by CSV, so
    they are coerced back to float on load and the PSD round-trips. Shared
    with the aperiodic-removed twin so `compute_psd` runs once per modality.
    """
    path = CACHE_DIR / f"{name}.csv"
    if path.exists():
        df = pd.read_csv(path, index_col=0)
        df.columns = [float(c) if _is_float_str(c) else c for c in df.columns]
        return df
    df = build()
    df.to_csv(path)
    return df


def freq_cols(df: pd.DataFrame, fmin: float = 0.0) -> np.ndarray:
    """Sorted float (frequency) column labels >= `fmin`."""
    return np.array(sorted(c for c in df.columns if isinstance(c, float) and c >= fmin))
```

```{python}
#| label: load
def _build_ieeg() -> pd.DataFrame:
    # normalize=False -> keep raw units; the relative-power helpers normalise.
    _, psd = prepare_psd(
        matfile=DATA_PATH_IEEG / "WakefulnessMatlabFile.mat",
        region_dict_file=DATA_PATH_IEEG / "RegionInformation.csv",
        frauscher_bandpass=False,
        normalize=False,
        freq_range=FREQ_RANGE,
    )
    return psd


def _build_hd() -> pd.DataFrame:
    sources_raw, sources_meta = load_sources(DATA_PATH_SOURCES)
    f, psd = compute_psd(
        sources_raw.get_data(),
        sources_raw.info["sfreq"],
        fmin=FREQ_RANGE[0],
        fmax=FREQ_RANGE[1],
    )
    return pd.DataFrame(
        psd, index=pd.Index(sources_raw.ch_names, name="ch_name"), columns=f
    ).join(sources_meta)


ieeg_psd = cache_csv("psd_ieeg_0p5_80", _build_ieeg)
hd_psd = cache_csv("psd_hd_0p5_80", _build_hd)
ieeg_f = freq_cols(ieeg_psd)
hd_f = freq_cols(hd_psd)
atlas = load_frauscher()
```

## Methods

#### Canonical-band and normalised relative-power maps

As a second, complementary approach, we mapped each region's normalised PSD onto the canonical bands defined above and took relative band power per region.

Relative band power does not separate the rhythmic peak from the aperiodic background, so it carries both: a region can show high relative band power because it has a strong rhythm or because its background is steep in that band [@donoghue2020ParameterizingNeuralPower@castanheira2025QuantifyingRhythmicArrhythmic].
Relative band powers are also compositional — within each region the five bands are normalised to a fixed total, so they are not free to vary independently [@filzmoser2012CorrelationAnalysisCompositional]. We therefore report the cross-modal correlations of these maps as descriptive measures of spatial agreement rather than as formal inference, and carry quantitative cross-modal inference with the aperiodic-separated peak descriptors, which are not subject to this closure.

### Quantitative descriptions 


#### Cross-modal correspondence on relative PSD spectra

This is the first of three cross-modal correspondence computations; the subtraction-based and modelled-peak versions are defined below and compared in @sec-concordance

We quantified cross-modal agreement on the unit-power PSDs using the band-overlap metric of @afnan2023ValidatingMEGSource. Channels were pooled across hemispheres by grouping on the hemisphere-agnostic MICCAI region name, collapsing left and right ROIs into the 38 bilateral regions of the atlas. Within each region $r$, we treated the iEEG atlas as the reference modality and the HD-EEG source data as the estimated modality. Let $\widetilde{L}_r(f)$ denote the median log-PSD across the channels of region $r$ at frequency bin $f$, and $\text{SD}^{\,\text{HD}}_r(f)$ the corresponding HD-EEG standard deviation. The bin-wise overlap is

$$
\text{overlap}_r(f) =
\begin{cases}
    1 - \dfrac{\bigl\lvert \widetilde{L}^{\,\text{iEEG}}_r(f) - \widetilde{L}^{\,\text{HD}}_r(f) \bigr\rvert}
              {\text{SD}^{\,\text{HD}}_r(f)},
        & \bigl\lvert \widetilde{L}^{\,\text{iEEG}}_r(f) - \widetilde{L}^{\,\text{HD}}_r(f) \bigr\rvert
          \le \text{SD}^{\,\text{HD}}_r(f) \\[2mm]
    0,  & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
$$


The metric equals 1 when the iEEG median lands exactly on the HD-EEG median and falls linearly to 0 once the two medians differ by one HD-EEG standard deviation. We averaged the bin-wise overlap across the frequency bins of each canonical band, giving one value per region per band, and report both the bin-level and the band-averaged overlap. To complement the overlap, we also rank-correlated the regional band estimates between modalities across regions (Spearman).

We also recomputed the overlap on the 22 data-driven Frauscher intervals [@frauscher2018AtlasNormalIntracranial], which give a more fine-grained view than the five canonical bands.

### Relative power after specparam aperiodic part removal 


We asked whether separating periodic from aperiodic activity changes the above picture. We addressed it in two linked ways: by modelling oscillatory peaks directly with specparam, and by removing the aperiodic background and recomputing the cross-modal overlap.

Each channel's PSD was parameterised with specparam, the spectral parameterisation model of @donoghue2020ParameterizingNeuralPower, fitted over 1-80 Hz with a peak configuration shared across both modalities: peak width limits of 1-8 Hz, at most 8 peaks, a minimum peak height of 0.1, and a peak threshold of 3 SD. Only the aperiodic component differed between modalities: it was modelled in the form chosen by the per-modality knee-versus-fixed BIC comparison (@sec-aperiodic-selection) — a knee model for the iEEG atlas and a fixed (knee-free) model for the source-reconstructed HD-EEG. From each fit we reconstructed the aperiodic component on the fitted frequency grid and subtracted it in linear power (next subsection), then normalised the residual to total power, so each band's oscillatory power is expressed as a fraction of total power and is directly comparable to the uncorrected relative band power above. One fit was produced per channel; goodness of fit and the fitted aperiodic parameters are reported in the Results.

We reconstructed the fitted aperiodic component on the fitted frequency grid and subtracted it from the empirical PSD in linear power space, giving the residual

$$\mathrm{PSD}_{\mathrm{osc}}(f) = \mathrm{PSD}(f) - \mathrm{PSD}_{\mathrm{ap}}(f).$$

This is the primary residual used throughout. We report a log-ratio alternative, $L_{\mathrm{osc}}(f) = \log_{10}(\mathrm{PSD}(f) / \mathrm{PSD}_{\mathrm{ap}}(f))$, which detrends in log space, the variant used for  detrending in many studies, as a sensitivity comparison.

Both residuals depend on the aperiodic fit, so error in the offset or exponent propagates into the oscillatory estimate; @castanheira2025QuantifyingRhythmicArrhythmic show this produces biased oscillatory power, more so in log space. Because we select the aperiodic mode per modality (knee vs fixed, @sec-aperiodic-selection), the iEEG and HD-EEG residuals are produced by different aperiodic models.

#### Assessing the overlap: reliability and rhythm presence

The band-overlap of @afnan2023ValidatingMEGSource is a *descriptive* agreement metric: on its own it indicates neither whether the agreement is statistically reliable nor whether there is a rhythm present to agree about — two flat residuals coincide and score an overlap near 1, a spurious agreement. We therefore assess the overlap in two complementary ways. Both are subject-clustered bootstraps with whole subjects resampled with replacement (iEEG `patient`, HD `dataset`; B = 2000), but they target different quantities and answer different questions.

We deliberately use a subject-clustered bootstrap rather than the channel-wise Welch *t*-test of @afnan2023ValidatingMEGSource, for three reasons specific to our design. First, our channels are nested in a small number of subjects (the source-reconstructed HD-EEG comprises only 19 subjects, each contributing many channels), and source leakage makes neighbouring source-space channels strongly correlated; a *t*-test on channels treats them as independent and so inflates the effective sample size from ~19 to several hundred, anti-conservatively shrinking the standard error. Welch's correction addresses unequal *variance*, not this non-independence, so it does not remedy the problem — whereas resampling whole subjects respects the nesting and keeps the exchangeable unit (the subject) as the unit of inference. Second, relative band power is bounded and the aperiodic-removed residual has a point mass at zero, violating the normality the *t*-test leans on at this sample size; the bootstrap is distribution-free. Third, and most directly, the overlap is a single statistic *derived* from both modalities, not a contrast between two samples, so a two-sample *t*-test does not apply to it at all — the only way to attach uncertainty to the overlap is to resample and recompute it. The reference (iEEG) modality is resampled too, since the atlas medians are themselves estimated from a finite set of patients.

The first assesses the **reliability of the overlap value**. We resample subjects in both modalities, recompute the band-overlap on each draw, and take a 95% percentile confidence interval per region and band; cells whose interval includes 0 are masked (shown in grey; @fig-overlap-pair-corrected). This asks *is the measured agreement reliably above zero?* Because the metric is bounded in $[0,1]$ and has no chance or permutation baseline, it is a reliability check — that the value is robust rather than zero by sampling noise — not a test against a null of no correspondence. It is also band-width dependent: averaging a non-negative metric over a wide canonical band drives its lower confidence bound above zero almost everywhere, so the five canonical bands leave far fewer cells masked than the 22 narrow Frauscher intervals, and the two band schemes are not directly comparable on this criterion.

The second assesses whether **a rhythm is present to be compared**, using the iEEG atlas as the reference (the ground truth). We bootstrap the aperiodic-removed band power per region and band and consider a region to carry a rhythm in a band when its mean residual power reliably exceeds zero (95% CI > 0). The overlap is then shown only where *both* modalities carry a rhythm; cells are masked where neither does (the overlap is uninterpretable — there is no oscillation to recover), and marked with a cross where the iEEG atlas carries a rhythm that HD-EEG fails to recover (@fig-overlap-corr-presence-gated-pair). This addresses the validation question directly: *where does source-reconstructed HD-EEG recover a genuine iEEG rhythm, and where does it miss one?* Presence here is significant oscillatory power above the $1/f$ background, a more permissive criterion than a fitted specparam peak.

The two analyses are complementary — the first measures how trustworthy the agreement value is, the second whether the agreement concerns real oscillatory structure — so we read the presence-conditioned map as the primary validation summary, because it separates genuine rhythm recovery from the spurious agreement of two flat residuals, and the confidence-interval map as a check on the metric itself. Both use the same display, differing only in the masking rule, and we show each band scheme (canonical bands, Frauscher intervals) side by side (@fig-overlap-pair-corrected, @fig-overlap-corr-presence-gated-pair).

Model fits were evaluated using R² and mean absolute error; fits with R² below 0.90 were excluded.




## Results




#### Band-power map and cross-modal overlap

We present regional relative band power, compared across modalities with the band-overlap metric.



Regional relative-power maps agreed across modalities most strongly in the alpha band (r = 0.60) and, more weakly, in the delta band (r = 0.42). Theta showed essentially no cross-modal correspondence (r = 0.13), beta only weak agreement (r = 0.30), and gamma was anti-correlated (r = −0.29). The spatial organisation of relative power is therefore only partially preserved between the iEEG atlas and source-reconstructed HD-EEG, and the preservation is band-dependent: it is confined largely to the alpha and low-frequency ranges that carry the clearest oscillatory structure, and breaks down at high frequencies. The negative gamma correlation is consistent with the high-frequency HD-EEG signal being dominated by a shallow aperiodic tail and noise floor rather than by physiological gamma — the same mechanism that drove the spurious gamma over-segmentation in the interval analysis — so that regions ranked high in HD-EEG gamma relative power are not those ranked high in the atlas. Relative to the identity line

Points are coloured by lobe, the solid line is the per-band OLS fit, and the dashed line marks identity (y = x). Strip labels give the per-band Pearson](figures/chapter2/uncorrected/relpower_scatter_uncorrected.pdf){#fig-relpower-scatter-uncorrected}

These per-band correlations should be read as descriptive rather than inferential. Relative band powers are *compositional*: within each channel they are normalised to a fixed total, so the five bands are not independent and an increase in one band necessarily depresses the others. This closure constraint induces negative coupling between bands by construction — part of the negative gamma correlation is therefore arithmetic rather than physiological — and it violates the independence assumptions of ordinary correlation and t-tests applied to the raw proportions[@filzmoser2012CorrelationAnalysisCompositional]. Valid inference would require analysing the maps in a log-ratio space (e.g. centred or isometric log-ratio transforms), which also removes any dependence on the per-channel normalisation choice. We retain the untransformed maps here as a descriptive summary and defer formal cross-modal inference to the aperiodic-separated peak descriptors below, which are not subject to the same closure.


In @fig-relpower-maps-uncorrected we present results on scalp.

```{python}
#| label: fig-overlap
# Afnan band-overlap on the unit-power PSDs: iEEG as reference, HD-EEG as
# estimate, grouped on the bilateral MICCAI region name (default region_col).
overlap_raw = afnan_band_overlap(
    ref_df=relative_psd_df(ieeg_psd, ieeg_f),
    est_df=relative_psd_df(hd_psd, hd_f),
    ref_freqs=ieeg_f,
    est_freqs=hd_f,
)
# Render the per-band overlap as cortical maps — one panel per canonical band,
# laid out horizontally like @fig-relpower-maps-uncorrected — instead of a heatmap.
# Each region's bilateral overlap is mapped onto the Frauscher atlas by its
# frauscher_id and shown on a FIXED 0-1 colour scale: the metric is already in

from ggsegpy.geom_brain import geom_brain
from plotnine import (
    aes,
    element_blank,
    element_text,
    facet_grid,
    ggplot,
    scale_fill_cmap,
    theme,
    theme_gray,
)
from plotnine.facets.labelling import labeller

from pesco.spectral import EEG_BANDS

OVERLAP_BANDS = [(b.name, b.lo, b.hi) for b in EEG_BANDS]
name_to_fid = dict(zip(ieeg_psd["Region name"], ieeg_psd["ChannelRegion"]))

overlap_roi.insert(0, "frauscher_id", [name_to_fid[r] for r in overlap_roi.index])

# Per-band mean overlap across regions, written into the facet strip. The "i · "
# prefix only orders the facets and is stripped back off by the labeller.
band_mean = overlap_raw.mean()
band_facet = {
    name: f"{i} · {name} ({lo:g}-{hi:g} Hz)\nmean {band_mean[name]:.2f}"
    for i, (name, lo, hi) in enumerate(OVERLAP_BANDS)
}
overlap_long["band_facet"] = overlap_long["band"].astype(str).map(band_facet)
overlap_long = overlap_long[["label", "value", "band_facet"]]


def _strip(s):
    return s.split(" · ", 1)[1]


overlap_brain = (
    ggplot(overlap_long, aes(fill="value"))
    + geom_brain(atlas=atlas, mapping=aes(fill="value"), hemi="left", show_legend=True)

        cmap_name="YlGnBu",  # match the Frauscher-bin overlap heatmaps

    )
    + theme_gray()

        strip_text=element_text(size=9, weight="bold", family="sans-serif"),

        legend_key_width=8,

        plot_margin=0.01,
    )
)
overlap_brain.save(
    fig_dir / "overlap_maps_uncorrected.pdf",
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-overlap-frauscher-bootci
# Frauscher-binned cross-modal overlap with a subject-clustered bootstrap CI on
# the metric itself (pesco.spectral.bootstrap_overlap_ci): whole subjects are
# resampled in BOTH modalities — the iEEG reference is a finite patient sample
# too — and the Afnan overlap is recomputed each draw (B=2000, cached). Cells
# whose 95% CI includes 0 are greyed (overlap not reliably > 0), as the
# clustering heatmap blanks non-significant cells. A contrast dot flags "similar
# but flat" cells — a reliable overlap with no bootstrap-significant rhythm in
# EITHER modality (spurious agreement); empty for uncorrected relative power
# (always present), it becomes informative on the aperiodic-removed residual.
# Shared FRAUSCHER_BANDS / REGION_LOBE / helpers are defined here and reused by
# the aperiodic-removed twin below.
import warnings

from pesco.bandpower import integrate_bands
from pesco.crossmodal import cluster_bootstrap_cell_means
from pesco.experimental.clustering import Band
from pesco.experimental.peak_testing import cutintervals
from pesco.experimental.plotting import plot_overlap_frauscher_heatmap
from pesco.spectral import bootstrap_overlap_ci

# Frauscher's 22 data-driven intervals (0.5-80 Hz; the cluster bins of 1a).
_, _fb_edges = cutintervals(ieeg_f)
FRAUSCHER_BANDS = [
    Band(float(lo), float(hi), f"{lo:g}-{hi:g}", "", float((lo + hi) / 2))
    for lo, hi in zip(_fb_edges[:-1], _fb_edges[1:])
]
FB_TUPLES = [(b.name, b.lo, b.hi) for b in FRAUSCHER_BANDS]
FB_NAMES = [b.name for b in FRAUSCHER_BANDS]
REGION_LOBE = (
    ieeg_psd[["Region name", "Lobe"]]
    .drop_duplicates()
    .set_index("Region name")["Lobe"]
    .to_dict()
)


def band_presence(df, freqs, regions, subjects, *, bands=FRAUSCHER_BANDS, B=2000, seed=3):
    """Bootstrap-significant (95% CI > 0) band power per region x band.

    Subject-clustered bootstrap of the mean band power across each region's
    channels; True where the lower CI excludes 0 (a rhythm is present). Works on
    raw relative PSD and on the oscillatory residual (NaN outside the fit range),
    and for any ``bands`` scheme (Frauscher intervals or canonical EEG bands).
    """
    tuples = [(b.name, b.lo, b.hi) for b in bands]
    names = [b.name for b in bands]
    bp = integrate_bands(df[list(freqs)].to_numpy(dtype=float), freqs, tuples)
    rcol = df["Region name"].to_numpy()
    subjects = np.asarray(subjects)
    out = pd.DataFrame(index=regions, columns=names, dtype=bool)
    for name in names:
        vals = bp[name].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        mat = np.full((len(vals), len(regions)), np.nan)
        for j, r in enumerate(regions):
            mat[rcol == r, j] = vals[rcol == r]
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
            _, lo, _ = cluster_bootstrap_cell_means(mat, subjects, B=B, seed=seed)
        out[name] = lo > 0.0
    return out


def overlap_ci_cached(tag, ref_df, est_df, ref_f, est_f, ref_subj, est_subj, *, bands=FRAUSCHER_BANDS):
    """`bootstrap_overlap_ci` over ``bands``, lo/hi cached as CSV under ``tag``."""
    lo_path = CACHE_DIR / f"overlap_boot_ci_lo_{tag}.csv"
    hi_path = CACHE_DIR / f"overlap_boot_ci_hi_{tag}.csv"
    if lo_path.exists() and hi_path.exists():
        point = afnan_band_overlap(ref_df, est_df, ref_f, est_f, bands=bands)
        return point, pd.read_csv(lo_path, index_col=0), pd.read_csv(hi_path, index_col=0)
    point, lo, hi = bootstrap_overlap_ci(
        ref_df, est_df, ref_f, est_f, ref_subj, est_subj, bands=bands, seed=3
    )
    lo.to_csv(lo_path)
    hi.to_csv(hi_path)
    return point, lo, hi


def overlap_frauscher_masks(ci_lo, pres_ref, pres_est, regions, *, names=FB_NAMES):
    """(grey, dot) masks: grey = CI includes 0; dot = reliable overlap but flat.

    Gating built on the *overlap* bootstrap (bootstrap_overlap_ci).
    """
    grey = ci_lo.reindex(regions)[names] <= 0.0
    flat_both = (
        (~pres_ref & ~pres_est).reindex(index=regions, columns=names).fillna(False)
    )
    return grey, flat_both & ~grey


def presence_gated_masks(pres_ref, pres_est, regions, *, names=FB_NAMES):
    """(grey, mark) masks — Option C, reference-gated on the *presence* bootstrap.

    Gating built on the peaks-presence bootstrap (``band_presence``), not the
    overlap bootstrap: the overlap colour is shown only where a significant
    rhythm exists in BOTH modalities; grey elsewhere, with ``mark`` (x) flagging
    region x band where the iEEG atlas carries a rhythm that HD-EEG did not
    recover. Swap this in for :func:`overlap_frauscher_masks` to change the
    gating while reusing the same renderer.
    """
    ref = pres_ref.reindex(index=regions, columns=names).fillna(False)
    est = pres_est.reindex(index=regions, columns=names).fillna(False)
    return ~(ref & est), ref & ~est


rel_ie = relative_psd_df(ieeg_psd, ieeg_f)
rel_hd = relative_psd_df(hd_psd, hd_f)
ie_subj = rel_ie["patient"].to_numpy()
# HD subject id lives in the channel name (datasetNN_...); `dataset` is constant.
```

```{python}
# Median relative band power per region (before aperiodic correction), as
# region x band heatmaps rather than cortical maps: four panels laid out
# horizontally — iEEG and HD-EEG, each in the 5 canonical bands and the 22

# is the MEDIAN across the region's channels of the within-band relative power.
from pesco.experimental.facets import overlap_heatmap_grid


def region_median_relpower(psd_df, freqs, bands):
    # band_fraction_by_channel = band power / total power per channel, so each
    # value is a fraction in [0, 1]; median across the region's channels.
    tuples = [(b.name, b.lo, b.hi) for b in bands]
    bf = band_fraction_by_channel(psd_df, freqs, "Region name", tuples)
    return bf.groupby("Region name")[[b.name for b in bands]].median()
```

#### Aperiodic-removed band power

The specparam model captured the aperiodic background well in the iEEG atlas: across the 1772 channels the knee model reached a mean R² of 0.98 (± 0.01; median 0.985, only 4 channels below 0.90), with a mean offset of 5.10 ± 1.57 and an exponent of 3.39 ± 0.88, and a median knee frequency of 11.2 Hz (IQR 7.8-15.9). The fixed model on the 1444 source-reconstructed HD-EEG channels fit less well and far more variably (mean R² 0.91 ± 0.11, median 0.94; 376/1444 channels, 26%, fell below 0.90), with a much lower offset (−2.79 ± 0.58) and a shallower exponent (0.94 ± 0.33). Mean absolute error was comparable across modalities (0.087 vs 0.073 in log₁₀ power). The substantially poorer and more dispersed HD-EEG fits, together with the shallow exponent, indicate that the HD-EEG aperiodic estimate — and hence its oscillatory residual — is less reliable than the iEEG one.



The same three views, repeated on the *periodic* part of the spectrum. Each channel is fit with `specparam` in its BIC-selected aperiodic mode (iEEG knee, HD-EEG fixed;), the fitted aperiodic component on narmalized spectrum is subtracted,   so the per-band value is the channel's oscillatory power in that band as a fraction of total power — directly comparable to the uncorrected relative band power above. One fit per modality feeds all three figures; the fitted residuals are cached so the fit runs once.

Removing the aperiodic background isolates the rhythmic peaks from the $1/f$ tail, so the correspondence is no longer inflated (or, in gamma, depressed) by the steepness of the background. The closure constraint still applies — the linear residual is normalised to total power — so these per-band correlations remain descriptive.

```{python}
#| label: resid-fit
from IPython.display import Markdown
from specparam import SpectralGroupModel

from pesco.bandpower import BAND_LABELS, add_roi_hemisphere_labels, integrate_bands
from pesco.config import FREQ_RANGE as FIT_RANGE, SELECTED_MODE, SPECPARAM_SETTINGS
from pesco.spectral import remove_aperiodic, specparam2pandas

fig_dir_corr = Path("figures/chapter2/corrected")
fig_dir_corr.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# Scatter/overlap bands keep the canonical 0.5 Hz delta edge; the fitted grid
# starts at FIT_RANGE[0] so the mask is identical in practice.
EEG_BAND_TUPLES = [
    ("δ", 0.5, 4.0),
    ("θ", 4.0, 8.0),
    ("α", 8.0, 13.0),
    ("β", 13.0, 30.0),
    ("γ", 30.0, 80.0),
]


def fit_residual_and_params(short, dataset, psd_df, freqs):
    """One specparam fit (BIC-selected mode) -> (residual, aperiodic params).

    Both outputs come from the same fit and are cached as CSV in `_cache/`, so
    the slow fit runs once: the normalised linear oscillatory residual (channel
    x frequency + metadata) and the per-channel aperiodic parameters extracted
    with `specparam2pandas` (offset, exponent, +knee in knee mode; with the fit
    R^2 / MAE).
    """
    resid_path = CACHE_DIR / f"resid_{short}_linear.csv"
    ap_path = CACHE_DIR / f"aperiodic_params_{short}.csv"
    if resid_path.exists() and ap_path.exists():
        osc = pd.read_csv(resid_path, index_col=0)
        osc.columns = [float(c) if _is_float_str(c) else c for c in osc.columns]
        return osc, pd.read_csv(ap_path, index_col=0)

    fg = SpectralGroupModel(
        **SPECPARAM_SETTINGS, aperiodic_mode=SELECTED_MODE[dataset], verbose=False
    )
    fg.fit(
        np.asarray(freqs, dtype=float),
        psd_df[list(freqs)].to_numpy(dtype=float),
        freq_range=list(FIT_RANGE),
        n_jobs=1,
    )
    ffreqs, osc_mat = remove_aperiodic(fg, mode="linear")
    meta = [c for c in psd_df.columns if isinstance(c, str)]
    osc = pd.DataFrame(osc_mat, index=psd_df.index, columns=ffreqs).join(psd_df[meta])

    ap_cols = ["offset", "exponent"] + (
        ["knee"] if SELECTED_MODE[dataset] == "knee" else []
    )
    ap = (
        specparam2pandas(fg)
        .drop_duplicates("ID")  # one row per spectrum; aperiodic params repeat over peaks
        .set_index("ID")[ap_cols + ["error_mae", "gof_rsquared"]]
    )
    ap.insert(0, "channel", [psd_df.index[i] for i in ap.index])
    ap["dataset"] = dataset

    osc.to_csv(resid_path)
    ap.to_csv(ap_path)
    return osc, ap


ieeg_osc, ieeg_ap = fit_residual_and_params("ieeg", "iEEG atlas", ieeg_psd, ieeg_f)
hd_osc, hd_ap = fit_residual_and_params("hd", "source HD-EEG", hd_psd, hd_f)
ieeg_ff = freq_cols(ieeg_osc)
hd_ff = freq_cols(hd_osc)
```

The fitted aperiodic parameters summarise each modality's $1/f$ background — iEEG fit with a knee, HD-EEG with the fixed (knee-free) model. Offset and exponent are mean ± sd across channels; the knee is reported as the knee *frequency* ($\text{knee}^{1/\chi}$, in Hz) as median [IQR], since the raw knee parameter is heavy-tailed (a few channels push the knee out of band).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-aperiodic-params
#| output: true
def _ap_summary(ap, label):
    row = {"modality": label, "n channels": len(ap)}
    row["offset"] = f"{ap['offset'].mean():.3f} ± {ap['offset'].std():.3f}"
    row["exponent"] = f"{ap['exponent'].mean():.3f} ± {ap['exponent'].std():.3f}"
    if "knee" in ap:
        # knee frequency = knee^(1/exponent); median [IQR], robust to the
        # heavy-tailed raw knee param.
        fk = ap["knee"].clip(lower=0) ** (1.0 / ap["exponent"])
        row["knee freq (Hz)"] = (
            f"{fk.median():.2f} [{fk.quantile(.25):.2f}, {fk.quantile(.75):.2f}]"
        )
    else:
        row["knee freq (Hz)"] = "—"
    row["R² (mean)"] = f"{ap['gof_rsquared'].mean():.3f}"
    return row


ap_summary = pd.DataFrame(
    [_ap_summary(ieeg_ap, "iEEG (knee)"), _ap_summary(hd_ap, "HD-EEG (fixed)")]
).set_index("modality")[
    ["n channels", "offset", "exponent", "knee freq (Hz)", "R² (mean)"]
]
Markdown(ap_summary.to_markdown())
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-scatter-corr
# Per-channel oscillatory-residual band power -> tidy table matching
# relative_band_power_by_channel, so the raw pairing pipeline is reused.
def _resid_tidy(osc_df, ff, dataset):
    bs = integrate_bands(osc_df[list(ff)].to_numpy(dtype=float), ff, EEG_BAND_TUPLES)
    meta_cols = [c for c in ["Region name", "Lobe", "hemisphere", "mni_x"] if c in osc_df]
    meta = add_roi_hemisphere_labels(osc_df[meta_cols]).reset_index(drop=True)
    meta.insert(0, "channel", osc_df.index.astype(str))
    meta["dataset"] = dataset
    rows = []
    for name, _, _ in EEG_BAND_TUPLES:
        df = meta.copy()
        df["band"] = name
        df["band_label"] = BAND_LABELS[name]
        df["relative_power"] = bs[name].to_numpy()
        rows.append(df)
    return pd.concat(rows, ignore_index=True)


resid_by_channel = pd.concat(
    [_resid_tidy(ieeg_osc, ieeg_ff, "iEEG atlas"), _resid_tidy(hd_osc, hd_ff, "source HD-EEG")],
    ignore_index=True,
)
resid_region = region_band_power(resid_by_channel, summary="mean", roi_level="bilateral")
resid_paired, resid_corr = compare_region_band_power(
    resid_region,
    x_dataset="source HD-EEG",
    y_dataset="iEEG atlas",
    roi_col="roi_bilateral",
    n_label="n_regions",
)
plot_band_grid = plot_band_power_correlation_grid(
    resid_paired,
    resid_corr,
    color_by="lobe",
    method="pearson",
    identity_line=True,
    x_label="source HD-EEG\noscillatory residual",
    y_label="iEEG atlas\noscillatory residual",
    title="Aperiodic-removed: bilateral regional oscillatory-residual correspondence",
)
plot_band_grid.save(
    fig_dir_corr / "relpower_scatter_corrected.pdf",
    verbose=False,
)
plot_band_grid
```

```{python}
def _resid_roi(osc_df, ff, region_col):
    bands = integrate_bands(osc_df[list(ff)].to_numpy(dtype=float), ff, MAP_BANDS)
    bands[region_col] = osc_df[region_col].to_numpy()

        bands.groupby(region_col)[MAP_BAND_ORDER]

    )
```

```{python}
    left_title="Canonical bands",
    right_title="Frauscher intervals",
    suptitle="iEEG vs HD-EEG overlap (aperiodic-removed)\n"
    "grey = 95% CI includes 0 · dot = reliable overlap but flat (spurious agreement)",
)
fig.savefig(
    fig_dir_corr / "overlap_pair_corrected.pdf", bbox_inches="tight", dpi=300
)
fig.savefig(
    fig_dir_corr / "overlap_pair_corrected.svg", bbox_inches="tight", dpi=300
)
fig
```

![Aperiodic-removed cross-modal overlap. A) five canonical EEG bands B)the 22 intervals defined in @frauscher2018AtlasNormalIntracranial.  Both panels are masked (grey) where the bootstrap 95% CI of the overlap includes 0 and carry a contrast dot where a reliable overlap sits on a flat residual (no significant rhythm in either modality — spurious agreement).](figures/chapter2/corrected/overlap_pair_corrected.pdf){#fig-overlap-pair-corrected}

#### Presence-conditioned overlap (peaks-presence bootstrap)

As an alternative to conditioning on the overlap's own confidence interval, we condition on whether a rhythm is actually present. This is the same subject-clustered bootstrap of the oscillatory-residual band power used above (`band_presence`, 95% CI > 0), but here it drives a view of the canonical-band overlap referenced to the iEEG atlas: only the mask-builder changes (`presence_gated_masks` instead of `overlap_frauscher_masks`), the overlap, presence and renderer are reused.

```{python}
#| label: fig-overlap-corr-presence-gated-optionc
# Option C — reference-gated presence. Reuses the canonical residual overlap and
# the peaks-presence bootstrap (pres_ie_canon / pres_hd_canon) computed above;
# only the mask-builder differs (presence_gated_masks), so the bootstrap/gating
# TYPE is swapped while the overlap + renderer are reused. Grey = no significant
# rhythm in BOTH modalities (overlap shown only where both carry one); x = iEEG
# carries a rhythm that HD-EEG did not recover.
grey_optionc, mark_optionc = presence_gated_masks(
    pres_ie_canon, pres_hd_canon, regions_canon, names=EEG_NAMES
)
fig, _ = plot_overlap_frauscher_heatmap(
    overlap_corr,
    REGION_LOBE,
    grey=grey_optionc,
    mark=mark_optionc,
    band_order=EEG_NAMES,
    xlabel="Frequency band",
    title="iEEG vs HD-EEG overlap (aperiodic-removed, canonical bands)\n"
    "presence-conditioned · grey = no rhythm in both · x = iEEG rhythm not recovered by HD",
)

# fig
```



```{python}
#| label: fig-overlap-corr-presence-gated-pair
# Presence-gated Option C, the two band schemes side by side via compose_panels:
# 5 canonical bands | 22 Frauscher bins. Reuses the canonical masks computed
# above (grey_optionc / mark_optionc) and builds the Frauscher ones from the
# Frauscher-bin presence (pres_ie_corr / pres_hd_corr) with the SAME mask-builder
# (presence_gated_masks) — only the band scheme differs.
from pesco.experimental.facets import overlap_heatmap_pair

grey_fb_optionc, mark_fb_optionc = presence_gated_masks(
    pres_ie_corr, pres_hd_corr, regions_corr, names=FB_NAMES
)
fig, _ = overlap_heatmap_pair(
    overlap_corr,
    overlap_corr_fb,
    REGION_LOBE,
    left_grey=grey_optionc,
    left_mark=mark_optionc,
    right_grey=grey_fb_optionc,
    right_mark=mark_fb_optionc,
    left_title="Canonical bands",
    right_title="Frauscher intervals",
    suptitle="iEEG vs HD-EEG overlap (aperiodic-removed) — presence-conditioned\n"
    "grey = no rhythm in both · x = iEEG rhythm not recovered by HD",
)
fig.savefig(
    fig_dir_corr / "overlap_pair_corrected_presencegated.pdf", bbox_inches="tight", dpi=300
)

fig
```
